_metadata.description: Questionnaire seed data loaded by DatabaseInitializer. Each entry creates a Questionnaire and (for native mode) its QuestionnaireFields. External-mode entries have an external_url and no sections/fields.

merge_tokens.{erName}: Employer name from activity's primary contact

questionnaires.name: NDT - Section 125 Cafeteria Plan Test
questionnaires.description: This questionnaire collects the data needed to perform nondiscrimination testing for a Section 125 cafeteria plan. Depending on the benefits offered, this may include Section 125 eligibility, contributions & benefits, and key employee concentration tests, as well as Section 105(h) self-insured plan tests and Section 129 dependent care tests. Sections will be marked as not applicable based on your answers.

sections.section_description: Tell us about the company sponsoring the plan and the plan year being tested.|Common mistakes: Using a trade name instead of the legal entity name. Entering the wrong plan year end date.

fields.label: Employer legal name
fields.help_text: Enter the legal name of the entity that sponsors the cafeteria plan.

fields.label: Plan year end date
fields.help_text: Enter the last day of the plan year being tested.

fields.label: Entity type
fields.help_text: Select the legal entity type of the plan sponsor. If the employer is part of a controlled group with mixed entity types, select the entity type of the entity that sponsors the cafeteria plan.

sections.section_name: Section B - Controlled Group / Affiliated Service Group
sections.section_description: We need to know if your company is related to other companies. If so, employees of ALL related companies count for testing, even if they cannot join the plan.|Common mistakes: Forgetting about companies owned by the same person or family. Not counting employees at sister companies.

fields.label: Is the employer part of a related group of companies?
fields.help_text: Related entities include parent-subsidiary groups (80%+ ownership), brother-sister groups (common ownership by 5 or fewer individuals), and affiliated service groups (service organizations with shared ownership or service relationships).

fields.label: Do any related companies exclude employees from the plan?
fields.help_text: Employees of non-covered related entities must still be included in the nondiscrimination testing population even though they cannot participate in the plan.

fields.label: Names of related companies whose employees cannot join
fields.help_text: Include every related entity in the group whose employees cannot enroll in the cafeteria plan.

fields.label: Total employees at those non-covered companies
fields.help_text: Count all common-law employees who were employed on any day during the plan year at the non-covered related entities listed above.

sections.section_description: Tell us about the plan sponsor's workforce size and union status. These numbers form the baseline for all testing calculations.|Common mistakes: Including independent contractors or leased employees in the count. Forgetting to check whether union benefits were actually bargained for.

fields.label: Total employees
fields.help_text: Count all common-law employees who were employed on any day during the plan year. Do not include independent contractors, leased employees, or employees of related entities (those are captured separately).

fields.label: Are any employees union members (covered by a CBA)?
fields.help_text: Employees covered by a CBA may be excludable from testing if cafeteria plan benefits were the subject of good-faith bargaining.

fields.label: Were cafeteria benefits bargained for in the CBA?
fields.help_text: CBA employees can only be excluded from testing if cafeteria plan benefits were actually bargained for in the agreement. If unsure, check the collective bargaining agreement or contact your labor counsel.

fields.label: Number of CBA-covered employees
fields.help_text: Count all common-law employees covered by the collective bargaining agreement(s).

fields.label: Can CBA employees participate in the cafeteria plan?
fields.help_text: CBA employees may be excludable from the testing population, but if they are eligible and participating, their elections still count in certain test calculations.

sections.section_description: Select the benefits available under the cafeteria plan. Your answers determine which tests apply and which sections you need to complete.|Common mistakes: Forgetting to include pre-tax premium deductions (POP). Not listing HSA contributions run through the cafeteria plan.

fields.label: Which benefits does the cafeteria plan offer?
fields.help_text: Select all benefits available to employees through the cafeteria plan. Pre-tax insurance premiums (POP) means employees can pay their share of employer-sponsored health, dental, or vision premiums on a pre-tax basis.
fields.select_options: Pre-tax insurance premiums (POP)|Health FSA|Limited Purpose FSA|Dependent Care FSA|HSA contributions|Other

fields.label: If Other, describe
fields.help_text: Describe any additional benefits offered through the cafeteria plan not listed above.

sections.section_name: Section F - Simple Cafeteria Plan Safe Harbor
sections.section_description: Small employers may qualify for a safe harbor that skips all testing. If your employer adopted this and meets the requirements, no further sections are needed.|Common mistakes: Assuming you qualify without confirming the plan document actually adopted the safe harbor. Not checking the 100-employee average over both prior years.

fields.label: Has the employer adopted a Simple Cafeteria Plan?
fields.help_text: A Simple Cafeteria Plan is a special safe harbor for small employers. Your plan document or benefits advisor can confirm whether this has been adopted.

fields.label: Did the employer average 100 or fewer employees?
fields.help_text: Only employers averaging 100 or fewer employees during both of the two preceding plan years are eligible for the Simple Cafeteria Plan safe harbor.

fields.label: Does the employer meet the contribution requirement?
fields.help_text: The Simple Cafeteria Plan requires the employer to meet one of these contribution requirements. Check your plan document for the contribution formula.

fields.label: Are all employees with 1,000+ hours eligible?
fields.help_text: The Simple Cafeteria Plan requires that all employees meeting the 1,000-hour threshold be eligible. Standard excludable employee rules (under age 21, CBA, nonresident alien) still apply.

sections.section_description: Tell us the plan's eligibility rules -- waiting periods, age limits, and hours requirements. These determine who can be excluded from testing.|Common mistakes: Reporting the insurance carrier's waiting period instead of the plan document's. Not realizing eligibility differs by employee class.

fields.label: Does the plan have a waiting period?
fields.help_text: If the plan requires employees to complete a waiting period before they can enroll, employees who have not yet met that requirement may be excludable from testing.

fields.label: How long is the waiting period?
fields.help_text: For nondiscrimination testing, employees with less than the plan's service requirement (up to 3 years) may be excluded from the testing population.
fields.select_options: 30 days|60 days|90 days|6 months|1 year|2 years|3 years|Other

fields.label: Does the plan require a minimum age?
fields.help_text: If the plan has a minimum age requirement, employees under that age may be excludable from testing.

fields.label: What is the minimum age?
fields.help_text: Employees under this age who are not yet eligible may be excluded from testing. The maximum excludable age is 21 under Section 125 proposed regulations.

fields.label: Does the plan require minimum hours worked?
fields.help_text: Part-time and seasonal employees may be excludable from testing if the plan imposes an hours or months-worked requirement.

fields.label: What is the hours requirement?
fields.help_text: Under Section 125, employees who worked fewer than 1,000 hours in the preceding plan year may be excluded. Under Section 105(h), the threshold is 35 hours per week.
fields.select_options: 500 hours per year|1,000 hours per year|Other

fields.label: Do eligibility rules differ by employee class?
fields.help_text: For example, salaried employees eligible immediately but hourly employees subject to a 90-day waiting period. If eligibility conditions differ by group, this affects how the eligibility test is evaluated.

fields.label: Describe the classes and their eligibility rules
fields.help_text: List each employee classification and the eligibility conditions that apply to it (e.g., 'Salaried - eligible immediately; Hourly - 90-day waiting period; Seasonal - not eligible').

sections.section_description: Count employees who can be left out of Section 125 testing. Only exclude employees if the plan itself imposes the matching eligibility condition from Section E.|Common mistakes: Excluding employees when the plan has no corresponding rule. Entering a count for a category that does not apply to your plan.

fields.label: Employees not yet meeting the service requirement
fields.help_text: Count employees who have not yet completed the plan's waiting period as reported in Section E. If the plan has no waiting period, enter 0. Employees can only be excluded if the plan imposes this requirement.

fields.label: Employees under the minimum age requirement
fields.help_text: Count employees under the minimum age reported in Section E. If the plan has no minimum age requirement, enter 0.

fields.label: Part-time or seasonal employees (under 1,000 hours)
fields.help_text: Count employees who worked fewer than 1,000 hours during the preceding plan year, or who worked during fewer than 7 months of the preceding plan year.

fields.label: Nonresident aliens with no US-source income
fields.help_text: Count employees who are nonresident aliens and receive no earned income from US sources from this employer. If none, enter 0.

fields.label: Employees on COBRA continuation coverage
fields.help_text: Count individuals receiving benefits under COBRA continuation provisions. If none, enter 0.

sections.section_description: Identify highly compensated individuals (HCIs) for Section 125 testing. Count everyone who qualifies across all related companies -- we handle eligibility exclusions later.|Common mistakes: Forgetting family attribution rules for ownership. Not counting officers at related entities. Leaving out spouses or dependents of HCIs who also work at the company.

fields.label: Employees who are more-than-5% owners
fields.help_text: Count employees who directly or indirectly own more than 5% of voting power or value of stock (for corporations), or more than 5% of capital or profits interest (for partnerships/LLCs). Under family attribution rules, ownership by a spouse, children, grandchildren, or parents is treated as the employee's own. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Officers not already counted as 5%+ owners
fields.help_text: Count officers (president, vice president, secretary, treasurer, or any other corporate officer) who were not already included in the ownership count above. Under Section 125, any officer is a Highly Compensated Individual regardless of compensation.

fields.label: High earners not already counted as owners/officers
fields.help_text: For the 2026 plan year, count employees who earned more than $160,000 in 2025. For the 2025 plan year, the threshold is $155,000 based on 2024 compensation. Do not include anyone already counted as a more-than-5% owner or officer above. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Are any employees spouses/dependents of those above?
fields.help_text: This is unique to Section 125 - spouses and dependents of HCIs are themselves HCIs regardless of their own compensation or position. Do not count anyone already included above.

fields.label: Additional employees who are HCI spouses/dependents
fields.help_text: Count employees who are spouses or dependents of anyone identified in the questions above, and who have not already been counted in any prior question.

fields.label: Total HCIs (sum of all above)
fields.help_text: This should equal the sum of all HCI counts from the questions above. Because each category excluded prior counts, this total is already deduplicated.

fields.label: HCIs at non-covered related companies
fields.help_text: If the employer is part of a controlled group and has related entities whose employees are not eligible for the cafeteria plan, count HCIs at those entities. These individuals are HCIs who cannot participate, which affects the eligibility test ratios. If no controlled group or no non-covered entities, enter 0.

sections.section_description: Determine whether the plan is open to employees on equal terms. If all non-excludable employees have the same access, it passes automatically.|Common mistakes: Answering Yes when salaried and hourly employees actually have different waiting periods. Not subtracting excludable employees before calculating totals.

fields.label: Is the plan open to all eligible employees equally?
fields.help_text: If every non-excludable employee has the same eligibility conditions and access to the same benefits, the plan automatically passes the Section 125 eligibility test. Answer No if any group of employees has different eligibility conditions, waiting periods, or benefit access than another group.

fields.label: Describe how eligibility differs by group
fields.help_text: Describe which employees are eligible and which are not, and the business criteria used (e.g., 'All salaried employees are eligible; hourly warehouse employees are not eligible'). The classification must be based on reasonable, objective business criteria such as job category, salaried vs. hourly, geographic location, division, or business unit.

fields.label: Total non-excludable employees
fields.help_text: Start with total employees across all related entities, then subtract excludable employees (those reported in Section G who meet a plan eligibility condition). This is the testing population.

fields.label: Non-HCIs eligible to participate
fields.help_text: Of all non-excludable non-HCI employees, how many are actually eligible to participate in the cafeteria plan?

sections.section_name: Section O - Section 125 Contributions & Benefits Test
sections.section_description: Check whether benefits and employer contributions favor highly compensated participants. Skip this section if the plan only offers pre-tax premium deductions (POP only).|Common mistakes: Including employer contributions in the employee salary reduction total. Confusing HCIs (identified) with HCPs (those who actually elected benefits).

fields.label: Are the same benefits offered to everyone equally?
fields.help_text: All qualified benefits and employer contributions must be available on the same terms to all participants. The same benefits must be offered, the required employee contribution for each benefit level must be identical, and maximum benefit levels cannot vary based on compensation, age, or years of service.

fields.label: Describe how benefits or terms differ by group
fields.help_text: Explain which benefits, contribution levels, or maximum amounts differ and for which groups. For example, 'Executives receive an employer HSA contribution of $1,500; all other employees receive $750.'

fields.label: Does the employer contribution meet the 75% safe harbor?
fields.help_text: This is a safe harbor for health benefits (not FSAs). If the employer contributes at least 75% of the most expensive health option, the contributions and benefits test is deemed satisfied for those health benefits.
fields.select_options: Yes|No|Not applicable - no employer health contributions

fields.label: HCIs who elected benefits (HCPs)
fields.help_text: Count HCIs who actually made elections under the cafeteria plan - these are Highly Compensated Participants (HCPs). Include elections for any nontaxable benefit: pre-tax premiums, Health FSA, Dependent Care FSA, HSA contributions, etc.

fields.label: Non-HCIs who elected benefits
fields.help_text: Count non-HCI employees who actually made elections under the cafeteria plan.

fields.label: Total salary reductions elected by HCPs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of pre-tax salary reductions elected by all HCI participants. This is the employee-paid portion only - do not include employer contributions.

fields.label: Total employer contributions for HCPs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount the employer contributes toward benefits for all HCI participants. This includes the employer share of insurance premiums and any employer contributions to FSAs, HSAs, or HRAs.

fields.label: Total salary reductions elected by non-HCIs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of pre-tax salary reductions elected by all non-HCI participants. This is the employee-paid portion only.

fields.label: Total employer contributions for non-HCIs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount the employer contributes toward benefits for all non-HCI participants.

sections.section_description: Identify key employees for the Section 125 concentration test. Count everyone who qualifies across all related companies -- we handle eligibility exclusions later. Skip if the plan only offers POP.|Common mistakes: Confusing key employees with HCIs -- they use different definitions. Using the wrong compensation threshold year.

fields.label: Employees who are more-than-5% owners
fields.help_text: Count employees who directly or indirectly own more than 5% of the employer. This may be the same count as reported in the Section 125 HCI classification section. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: 1-5% owners earning over $150,000 (not counted above)
fields.help_text: Count employees who own more than 1% but not more than 5%, and who earned more than $150,000 in the preceding plan year. The $150,000 threshold is NOT indexed for inflation. Do not include anyone already counted as a >5% owner above. Include employees at all related entities.

fields.label: Officers above the comp threshold (not counted above)
fields.help_text: For the 2026 plan year, count officers who earned more than $230,000 in 2025. For the 2025 plan year, the threshold is $220,000 based on 2024 compensation. Do not include anyone already counted as a >5% or >1% owner above. Include officers at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Total key employees (sum of all above)
fields.help_text: This should equal the sum of all Key Employee counts from the questions above. Note: Key Employee status is different from HCI status - an employee can be one but not the other.

fields.label: Key employees at non-covered related companies
fields.help_text: Count Key Employees at related entities whose employees are not eligible for the cafeteria plan. If no controlled group or no non-covered entities, enter 0.

sections.section_name: Section P - Section 125 Key Employee Concentration Test
sections.section_description: Check whether key employees receive too large a share of plan benefits. No more than 25% of total nontaxable benefits can go to key employees. Skip if POP only.|Common mistakes: Including employer contributions when only employee salary reductions were requested. Not separating key employee amounts from the rest.

fields.label: Key employees who elected benefits
fields.help_text: Of the key employees identified in Section M, count those who actually made elections under the cafeteria plan. Key employees at non-covered related entities would not have elections.

fields.label: Total salary reductions by key employees
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of pre-tax salary reductions elected by all key employee participants. This is the employee-paid portion only - do not include employer contributions.

fields.label: Total employer contributions for key employees
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount the employer contributes toward benefits for all key employee participants. This includes the employer share of insurance premiums and any employer contributions to FSAs, HSAs, or HRAs.

sections.section_description: Count employees who can be left out of Section 105(h) testing. The thresholds differ from Section 125: age 25 (not 21), 35 hours/week (not 1,000/year), and 3 years of service. Applies only if a Health FSA or Limited Purpose FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Using Section 125 thresholds instead of Section 105(h) thresholds. Measuring service as of the wrong date (should be start of plan year).

fields.label: Employees with less than 3 years of service
fields.help_text: Count employees with fewer than 3 full years of service as of the first day of the plan year. This threshold applies regardless of the plan's own waiting period.

fields.label: Employees under age 25
fields.help_text: Count employees who had not reached age 25 as of the first day of the plan year. Note: this is age 25, not age 21 - the Section 105(h) threshold is different from Section 125.

fields.label: Employees working fewer than 35 hours per week
fields.help_text: Count employees who are customarily scheduled for fewer than 35 hours per week, or who worked fewer than 7 months in the preceding plan year. Note: this is 35 hours/week, not 1,000 hours/year - the Section 105(h) threshold is different from Section 125.

fields.label: Nonresident aliens with no US-source income
fields.help_text: Count employees who are nonresident aliens and receive no earned income from US sources from this employer. If none, enter 0. This count may be the same as reported in the Section 125 excludable employees section.

sections.section_description: Identify highly compensated individuals under the Section 105(h) definition, which differs from Section 125: top 5 officers (not all), 10%+ owners (not 5%), and top 25% by pay. Applies only if a Health FSA or Limited Purpose FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Using the Section 125 ownership threshold (5%) instead of 10%. Counting all officers instead of only the 5 highest-paid.

fields.label: Employees who are more-than-10% owners
fields.help_text: Count employees who directly or indirectly own more than 10% in value of the employer's stock, applying Section 318 family attribution rules. Note: this is a higher threshold than Section 125 (>10% vs. >5%), so fewer individuals may qualify. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Top-5 paid officers not counted as 10%+ owners
fields.help_text: Under Section 105(h), only the 5 highest-paid officers are HCIs - not all officers. Identify the 5 officers with the highest annual compensation and count those not already included as >10% owners. If the employer has fewer than 5 officers, count all of them (minus any already counted as owners).

fields.label: Top-25% earners not counted as owners/officers
fields.help_text: Rank all employees (excluding excludable non-participants) by current plan year compensation. Count those in the top 25% who were not already included as >10% owners or top-5 officers. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Total Section 105(h) HCIs (sum of all above)
fields.help_text: This should equal the sum of all Section 105(h) HCI counts from the questions above. Note: this number will likely differ from your Section 125 HCI total - the definitions are different.

fields.label: Section 105(h) HCIs at non-covered companies
fields.help_text: Count Section 105(h) HCIs at related entities whose employees are not eligible for the self-insured plan. If no controlled group or no non-covered entities, enter 0.

sections.section_description: Determine whether the self-insured plan (Health FSA) is open to employees fairly. Three sub-tests exist -- passing any one is enough. Applies only if a Health FSA or Limited Purpose FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Using Section 125 excludable counts instead of Section 105(h) counts. Confusing 'eligible to benefit' with 'actually benefiting.'

fields.label: Non-excludable employees who benefit under the plan
fields.help_text: For Health FSAs, 'benefit' means the employee elected to participate (made a salary reduction election). For HRAs/MERPs, 'benefit' means the employee is enrolled and covered. Do not count employees who are eligible but did not elect or enroll. Use Section 105(h) excludable employees (Section H) to determine your non-excludable population.

fields.label: Total non-excludable employees (Section 105(h) rules)
fields.help_text: Start with total employees across all related entities, then subtract Section 105(h) excludable employees reported in Section H (under age 25, less than 3 years of service, fewer than 35 hours/week, CBA, nonresident alien). This number may differ from the Section 125 non-excludable total because the thresholds are different.

fields.label: Non-excludable employees eligible to benefit
fields.help_text: Count all non-excludable employees who are offered the opportunity to participate, whether or not they elected to. This is everyone who could enroll if they chose to.

fields.label: Describe the eligibility classification
fields.help_text: Describe which employees are eligible and which are not, and the business criteria used (e.g., 'All full-time salaried employees are eligible; part-time and seasonal employees are not'). The classification must be based on reasonable, objective business criteria.

fields.label: Section 105(h) HCIs who benefit under the plan
fields.help_text: Of the Section 105(h) HCIs identified in Section K, how many actually benefit under the self-insured plan? For Health FSAs, this means they elected to participate.

fields.label: Non-excludable Section 105(h) HCIs
fields.help_text: Of all Section 105(h) HCIs (Section K), how many are in the non-excludable testing population?

fields.label: Non-HCIs who benefit under the plan
fields.help_text: Of all non-excludable non-HCI employees, how many actually benefit under the self-insured plan?

fields.label: Total non-excludable non-HCIs
fields.help_text: Total non-excludable employees (field above) minus non-excludable Section 105(h) HCIs.

sections.section_description: Check whether the self-insured plan's benefits are designed and run fairly. This is about what is available, not who has higher claims. Applies only if a Health FSA or Limited Purpose FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Thinking higher HCI claims alone cause a failure (they do not). Not realizing that mid-year benefit changes can cause discrimination.

fields.label: Are the same expenses reimbursable for everyone?
fields.help_text: All medical expenses covered for HCIs must also be covered for all other participants. For example, the plan cannot cover dental expenses for executives only.

fields.label: Describe the differences in covered expenses
fields.help_text: Explain which expenses are covered differently and for which groups.

fields.label: Is the max reimbursement the same for everyone?
fields.help_text: The maximum benefit level attributable to employer contributions cannot vary based on compensation, age, or years of service. For Health FSAs, this means the same maximum election is available to everyone.

fields.label: Describe how maximums differ
fields.help_text: Explain which groups have different maximums and what those amounts are.

fields.label: Are employee contributions the same for everyone?
fields.help_text: If employees must contribute to participate in the plan, the contribution amount must be the same for all participants. Differences in cost-sharing can cause a benefits test failure.
fields.select_options: Yes|No|Not applicable - no employee contributions required

fields.label: Describe how employee contributions differ
fields.help_text: Explain which groups pay different amounts and what those amounts are.

fields.label: Are waiting periods the same for everyone?
fields.help_text: If HCIs have a shorter waiting period than other employees, the plan discriminates on its face. For example, if management is eligible immediately but hourly employees wait 90 days, this is a benefits test issue.

fields.label: Describe how waiting periods differ
fields.help_text: Explain which groups have different waiting periods.

fields.label: Is dependent coverage the same for everyone?
fields.help_text: All dependent coverage available to HCIs must be available on the same basis for all other participants.

fields.label: Describe how dependent coverage differs
fields.help_text: Explain which groups have different dependent coverage terms.

fields.label: Are executive physicals offered to only some groups?
fields.help_text: Section 105(h) includes a specific exception allowing medical diagnostic procedures (routine exams, blood tests, X-rays) for a classification of employees without violating the benefits test. If yes, this may still be permissible - but it must be limited to diagnostic/preventive care for the employee only, not dependents.

fields.label: Were benefits changed mid-year affecting groups differently?
fields.help_text: A plan that covers a benefit while an HCI needs it and then drops coverage is discriminatory in operation. Similarly, terminating a plan or benefit in a way that disproportionately favors HCIs can cause a failure.

fields.label: Describe the change and which groups were affected
fields.help_text: Explain what benefit changed, when, and how it affected different groups of employees.

sections.section_description: Count employees who can be left out of Section 129 (Dependent Care) testing. The thresholds differ from Section 125 and 105(h): age 21, 1 year of service, and a $25,000 pay exclusion. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Using the wrong age or service threshold from another section. Not knowing about the $25,000 compensation exclusion for the average benefits test.

fields.label: Employees under age 21
fields.help_text: Count employees who had not reached age 21 during the plan year. These employees may be excluded only if the plan excludes them from participation.

fields.label: Employees with less than 1 year of service
fields.help_text: Count employees who have not completed 1 year of service. These employees may be excluded only if the plan excludes them from participation.

fields.label: Nonresident aliens with no US-source income
fields.help_text: Count employees who are nonresident aliens and receive no earned income from US sources from this employer. If none, enter 0.

fields.label: Employees earning less than $25,000
fields.help_text: For the Section 129 55% Average Benefits Test only, employees earning less than $25,000 who participate through salary reduction may be excluded from the calculation. This threshold is not indexed for inflation.

sections.section_description: Identify highly compensated employees (HCEs) for Section 129 testing. This definition differs from Section 125 and 105(h): only 5%+ owners and high earners count -- no officer or spouse/dependent prong. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Including officers as a separate HCE category (they are not HCEs under Section 129 unless they meet the ownership or pay threshold). Counting spouses/dependents as HCEs (Section 129 does not include them).

fields.label: More-than-5% owners (current or prior year)
fields.help_text: Count employees who directly or indirectly own more than 5% of the employer. This uses the same ownership threshold as Section 125 (>5%), but does NOT include spouses and dependents of owners in the HCE definition. Ownership is tested as of any time during the current or preceding plan year. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: High earners not counted as 5%+ owners
fields.help_text: For the 2026 plan year, count employees who earned more than $160,000 in 2025. For the 2025 plan year, the threshold is $155,000 based on 2024 compensation. Do not include anyone already counted as a more-than-5% owner above. Include employees at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Total Section 129 HCEs (sum of above)
fields.help_text: This should equal the sum of questions above. Note: this number may differ from your Section 125 HCI total because Section 129 does not include officers as a separate category and does not include spouses/dependents of HCEs.

fields.label: Section 129 HCEs at non-covered companies
fields.help_text: Count Section 129 HCEs at related entities whose employees are not eligible for the Dependent Care FSA. If no controlled group or no non-covered entities, enter 0.

sections.section_description: Determine whether the Dependent Care FSA is open to employees on equal terms. If all non-excludable employees have the same access, it passes automatically. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Using Section 125 or 105(h) non-excludable counts instead of Section 129 counts. Not recalculating the testing population with Section 129 thresholds.

fields.label: Is the Dependent Care FSA open to all equally?
fields.help_text: If every non-excludable employee has the same eligibility conditions and access to the Dependent Care FSA, the Section 129 eligibility test is satisfied. Answer No if any group of employees has different eligibility conditions or access.

fields.label: Describe how DCFSA eligibility differs by group
fields.help_text: Describe which employees are eligible for the Dependent Care FSA and which are not, and the business criteria used. The classification must be based on reasonable, objective business criteria such as job category, salaried vs. hourly, geographic location, division, or business unit.

fields.label: Total non-excludable employees (Section 129 rules)
fields.help_text: Start with total employees across all related entities, then subtract Section 129 excludable employees reported in Section I (under age 21, less than 1 year of service, CBA, nonresident alien). This number may differ from the Section 125 and Section 105(h) non-excludable totals because the thresholds are different.

fields.label: Non-HCEs eligible for the Dependent Care FSA
fields.help_text: Of all non-excludable non-HCE employees (using the Section 414(q) HCE definition from Section L), how many are actually eligible to participate in the Dependent Care FSA?

sections.section_name: Section T - Section 129 Benefits & Contributions Test
sections.section_description: Check whether the Dependent Care FSA's benefits and terms are designed fairly for all eligible employees. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Not knowing the statutory max increased to $7,500 for 2026. Forgetting to report employer-paid (nonelective) DCAP contributions separately.

fields.label: Is the same DCFSA maximum available to everyone?
fields.help_text: All eligible employees must have access to the same maximum DCAP benefit. For the 2026 plan year, the statutory maximum is $7,500 (increased from $5,000 by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025). For 2025 and prior, the maximum is $5,000 ($2,500 for married filing separately).

fields.label: Describe how DCFSA maximums differ
fields.help_text: Explain which groups have different maximums and what those amounts are.

fields.label: Are DCFSA terms the same for all employees?
fields.help_text: This includes eligibility timing, enrollment procedures, reimbursement procedures, and any other plan terms. All participants must be treated the same.

fields.label: Describe how DCFSA terms differ
fields.help_text: Explain which terms differ and for which groups.

fields.label: Does the employer contribute to the DCFSA directly?
fields.help_text: If the employer contributes to the DCAP on behalf of employees (beyond salary reduction), those contributions must be available on a nondiscriminatory basis.

fields.label: Are employer contributions the same for everyone?
fields.help_text: Employer contributions must not favor HCEs. The same amount or formula must apply to all eligible employees.

fields.label: Describe the employer contribution structure
fields.help_text: Explain the contribution formula or amount and whether it varies by any factor.

sections.section_name: Section U - Section 129 More-Than-5% Owners Test
sections.section_description: Check whether 5%+ owners receive too large a share of Dependent Care benefits. No more than 25% of total DCAP benefits can go to 5%+ owners and their families. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Forgetting to include DCFSA elections by spouses and dependents of owners. Not including owners at related companies in the controlled group.

fields.label: 5%+ owners who elected DCFSA benefits
fields.help_text: Count more-than-5% owners who made a DCAP salary reduction election for the current plan year. Include owners at all related entities in the controlled group.

fields.label: Total DCFSA elections by 5%+ owners
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of DCAP salary reductions elected by all more-than-5% owner participants for the current plan year.

fields.label: Do owner spouses/dependents also have DCFSA elections?
fields.help_text: This test includes benefits provided to spouses and dependents of more-than-5% owners in the 25% concentration calculation. This includes spouses/dependents who are employees and have their own DCAP elections.

fields.label: Total DCFSA elections by owner spouses/dependents
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of DCAP salary reductions elected by spouses and dependents of more-than-5% owners. Do not include amounts already reported for the owners themselves.

fields.label: Total DCFSA elections for ALL participants
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of DCAP salary reductions elected by all DCAP participants for the current plan year - owners, spouses/dependents, and all other employees combined.

sections.section_name: Section V - Section 129 55% Average Benefits Test
sections.section_description: Check whether the average DCFSA benefit for non-HCEs is at least 55% of the average for HCEs. This is the test DCAPs fail most often. Applies only if a Dependent Care FSA is offered.|Common mistakes: Dividing by eligible employees instead of actual participants. Using Section 125 HCI counts instead of Section 129 HCE counts.

fields.label: HCEs who elected DCFSA benefits
fields.help_text: Count Section 414(q) HCEs (from Section L) who made a DCAP salary reduction election for the current plan year.

fields.label: Total DCFSA elections by HCEs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of DCAP salary reductions elected by all HCE participants for the current plan year.

fields.label: Non-HCEs who elected DCFSA benefits
fields.help_text: Count non-HCE employees who made a DCAP salary reduction election for the current plan year.

fields.label: Total DCFSA elections by non-HCEs
fields.help_text: Enter the total dollar amount of DCAP salary reductions elected by all non-HCE participants for the current plan year.

sections.section_description: Add any extra context and confirm your answers are accurate.|Common mistakes: Skipping helpful notes that would explain unusual numbers. Submitting without double-checking key totals.

fields.label: Additional notes or comments
fields.help_text: Use this space to provide any additional information, context, or explanations that may be relevant to the nondiscrimination testing.

fields.label: I confirm this information is accurate and complete
fields.help_text: By checking this box, you confirm that all responses reflect the current plan design and employee data as of the beginning of the plan year.
